results.title: Giant A counts as Strength only
Giant B, B-Upper and B-Lower count as Hypertrophy only
Athletic counts as Explosive and Capability, and NOT as Strength
Mobility counts as Low-intensity engine only, and NOT as Hypertrophy
Conditioning counts as High-intensity engine only
Block A variants (b2a…b7a) count as Strength only; block B variants (b2b…b7b, b3c) as Hypertrophy only
Optional bonus sessions count as Hypertrophy only (previously also Strength)
Practice and skill sessions whose purpose the source does not settle are not counted in any bar (Phase 2: Giant C now counts as Capability; see tests/phase2.test.js BU1-BU9 for the full model)
A mixed week totals correctly: A + B + athletic + conditioning + mobility
Training Budget page shows the corrected counts
Drafts and sessions older than 7 days are still excluded
Budget classification is read-only: stored sessions are unchanged
A check-in saved 1 hour ago is fresh: still GREEN with no stale warning (current behaviour preserved)
The freshness rule is the local calendar day (Phase 2 replaced the provisional 48-hour threshold): 2 h earlier the same day is fresh, 30 h earlier is stale
A GREEN check-in from 6 days ago is NOT shown as GREEN on Home; a visible stale warning gives its age
Never checked in (no saved date) shows NOT CHECKED IN instead of a YELLOW score
A stored joint flag is never hidden by staleness: joints 1/5 from 10 days ago still shows RED, with the stale note
Joints 2/5 from 10 days ago still shows YELLOW (not GREEN), with the stale note
A missing, null or unreadable date is treated as never checked in (no exception)
A check-in dated in the future (clock or time-zone change) is flagged, not trusted as fresh
Readiness page: stale check-in shows the warning and the age, and still offers SAVE CHECK-IN
Coach Handoff states the check-in is stale and how old it is, not an unqualified label
Saving a new check-in makes the status current immediately
readinessDecision itself is unchanged by staleness (classification guard from the reliability patch)
Rendering and classifying readiness never writes or alters stored data
Fresh check-ins of every joint level are classified exactly as before (no stale text anywhere)
Backup round trip preserves the saved readiness date, so staleness is the same after restore
When the restore fails AND putting the original data back also fails, the message does not claim the data was retained, and points to the snapshot
After that failure the pre-restore snapshot still holds ALL the original data and re-imports through the normal UI
When every write fails (not even a snapshot can be stored), restore is refused, nothing changes, and the message says so
A transient failure that the rollback survives still says the original data was retained, and storage is byte-identical
A normal successful restore is unchanged: reloads, replaces the data, keeps a snapshot
